cases.title: 1. Start an Original BOLD trial
cases.code:
library(BOLDx)
cfg <- bold_config(target=0.25, nmax=21, gamma=0.90, tau=0.50,
                   sensitivity=0.90, specificity=0.98, rho=0.80)
start <- plan_bold(history=NULL, ndoses=4, method="bold", config=cfg)
print(start$dose_recommendation)
print(start$ready)
cases.output:
Method: bold | Action: start | Next dose: 1
No patients enrolled; use the configured starting dose.
[1] TRUE
cases.interpretation: With no enrolled patients, Original BOLD assigns the configured starting dose. This is a next-cohort allocation, not a final MTD selection. True DLT risks are not supplied to a patient-history recommendation.

cases.title: 2. Enter a completed cohort and recommend the next dose
cases.code:
history <- data.frame(dose=c(1L,1L,1L), dlt=c(0L,0L,0L),
                      followup=c(3,3,3))
print(history)
original <- plan_bold(history, ndoses=4, current_dose=1,
                      method="bold", config=cfg)
print(original$dose_recommendation)
print(original$dose_recommendation$dose_summary, digits=4)
cases.output:
dose dlt followup
1    1   0        3
2    1   0        3
3    1   0        3
Method: bold | Action: escalate | Next dose: 2
Next cohort: dose 2 (escalate).
  dose n observed_dlts pending latent_intervention mean_untreated_risk
1    1 3             0       0                   0               0.125
2    2 0             0       0                   0               0.250
3    3 0             0       0                   0               0.250
4    4 0             0       0                   0               0.250
  overdose_probability excluded
1               0.1516    FALSE
2               0.4100    FALSE
3               0.4100    FALSE
4               0.4100    FALSE
cases.interpretation: Each row is an enrolled patient, in enrollment order. DLT=0 means no observed DLT; the three-month window is complete here. The dose summary reports untreated-risk estimates and overdose probabilities. Gamma is an elimination cutoff; tau is a separate BOLD decision target.

cases.title: 3. Add predictions and plan intervention for the incoming cohort
cases.code:
prediction_plan <- plan_bold(history, ndoses=4, current_dose=1,
  method="prediction", config=cfg,
  prediction=c(1L,0L,0L), eligible=c(TRUE,TRUE,TRUE))
print(prediction_plan$dose_recommendation)
print(prediction_plan$intervention_plan)
print(prediction_plan$ready)
cases.output:
Method: prediction | Action: escalate | Next dose: 2
Next cohort: dose 2 (escalate).
  prediction eligible intervene   status dose
1          1     TRUE      TRUE positive    2
2          0     TRUE     FALSE negative    2
3          0     TRUE     FALSE negative    2
[1] TRUE
cases.interpretation: Only the eligible incoming patient with prediction 1 is flagged for prevention. Incoming predictions do not change the historical posterior. If predictions depend on dose, obtain them at the candidate dose before acting. Sensitivity/specificity describe the external model; rho is used to generate interventions in simulation, not to replace actual history.

cases.title: 4. Record an actual intervention failure
cases.code:
failure_history <- transform(history, prediction=c(1L,0L,0L),
  eligible=TRUE, intervened=c(TRUE,FALSE,FALSE), dlt=c(1L,0L,0L))
print(failure_history)
failure <- plan_bold(failure_history, 4, 1, method="prediction", config=cfg,
                    prediction=c(0L,0L,0L))
print(failure$dose_recommendation)
print(failure$dose_recommendation$patient_status)
cases.output:
dose dlt followup prediction eligible intervened
1    1   1        3          1     TRUE       TRUE
2    1   0        3          0     TRUE      FALSE
3    1   0        3          0     TRUE      FALSE
Method: prediction | Action: stay | Next dose: 1
Next cohort: dose 1 (stay).
  patient dose          status
1       1    1    observed_dlt
2       2    1 observed_no_dlt
3       3    1 observed_no_dlt
cases.interpretation: The first patient received prevention and then had an observed DLT: this is a known failure, not an additional unresolved branch. Record only actual events and actual interventions. If prevention is followed by no DLT, untreated toxicity remains latent; it must not be entered as a known untreated non-DLT.

cases.title: 5. Update delayed outcomes in TITE-BOLD
cases.code:
pending <- data.frame(dose=c(1L,1L,1L), dlt=c(0L,0L,0L),
                      followup=c(3,3,1.5))
print(pending)
print(recommend_dose(pending, 4, 1, method="bold", config=cfg))
tite <- plan_bold(pending, 4, 1, method="tite", config=cfg)
print(tite$dose_recommendation)
print(tite$dose_recommendation$patient_status)
pending$followup[3] <- 3
print(recommend_dose(pending, 4, 1, method="tite", config=cfg))
cases.output:
dose dlt followup
1    1   0      3.0
2    1   0      3.0
3    1   0      1.5
Method: bold | Action: wait
Complete-follow-up mode: await all pending outcomes.
Method: tite | Action: escalate | Next dose: 2
Next cohort: dose 2 (escalate).
  patient dose          status
1       1    1 observed_no_dlt
2       2    1 observed_no_dlt
3       3    1         pending
Method: tite | Action: escalate | Next dose: 2
Next cohort: dose 2 (escalate).
cases.interpretation: Complete-follow-up BOLD waits for the third patient. TITE-BOLD can use partial follow-up, subject to its pending and escalation-readiness rules. Once that untreated patient completes follow-up, the observed non-DLT outcome replaces the pending contribution.

cases.title: 6. Combine prediction, prevention, and delayed outcomes
cases.code:
combined_history <- transform(pending, prediction=c(1L,0L,0L),
  eligible=TRUE, intervened=c(TRUE,FALSE,FALSE))
combined_history$followup <- c(1.5,3,3)
waiting <- plan_bold(combined_history, 4, 1, method="combined", config=cfg,
                     prediction=c(1L,0L,0L))
print(waiting$dose_recommendation)
print(waiting$intervention_plan)
combined_history$followup[1] <- 3
combined <- plan_bold(combined_history, 4, 1, method="combined", config=cfg,
                      prediction=c(1L,0L,0L))
print(combined$dose_recommendation)
print(combined$dose_recommendation$patient_status)
print(combined$intervention_plan)
cases.output:
Method: combined | Action: wait
Combined protocol: await intervention-patient outcome resolution.

2          0     TRUE     FALSE dose_wait   NA
3          0     TRUE     FALSE dose_wait   NA
Method: combined | Action: escalate | Next dose: 2
Next cohort: dose 2 (escalate).
  patient dose              status
1       1    1 latent_intervention
2       2    1     observed_no_dlt
3       3    1     observed_no_dlt
  prediction eligible intervene   status dose
1          1     TRUE      TRUE positive    2
2          0     TRUE     FALSE negative    2

cases.interpretation: Combined mode waits for intervention-patient outcome resolution. After a completed window with no DLT, that patient's counterfactual untreated status remains latent. Observed untreated outcomes replace pending predictions; an observed intervention failure is a known DLT. A wait/stop never schedules intervention.

cases.title: 7. Inspect the weighted Beta branches
cases.code:
mixture <- beta_mixture(a=0.75, b=2.25, q=c(1,1),
  labels=c(1L,1L), sensitivity=0.90, specificity=0.98, target=0.25)
print(mixture$components, digits=6)
print(c(mean=mixture$mean, overdose_probability=mixture$overdose_probability),
      digits=6)
cases.interpretation: These are the computed components for two latent positive-prediction patients at one dose. Equal-count branches are merged, so two binary splits yield three distinct Beta components rather than four unique Beta distributions. Weights sum to one. They encode possibilities, not extra patients.

cases.title: 8. Simulate one specified scenario with all six designs
cases.code:
methods <- c("bold","prediction","tite","combined","boin","tite_boin")
single <- simulate_bold(p.true=c(0.05,0.15,0.30,0.45,0.60),
  config=bold_config(target=0.30, nmax=21, gamma=0.90, tau=0.50,
    sensitivity=0.90, specificity=0.98, rho=0.80),
  method=methods, nsim=1000, seed=42, mtd=3)
print(single$summary, digits=5, row.names=FALSE)
print(single$mcse, digits=4, row.names=FALSE)
cases.interpretation: This risk vector is specified by the user, not randomly generated. Each design runs 1000 trials. MTD=3 affects evaluation only. Accuracy is the percent of trials selecting dose 3; actual DLTs are observed post-intervention events. Above-MTD allocation is patient-weighted. Duration is reported only for TITE designs. No method is forced to outperform others.

cases.title: 9. Generate 50 scenarios and run 1000 trials per design
cases.code:
panel <- simulate_random_scenarios(ndoses=4, mtd=2,
  lower_gap=0.10, upper_gap=0.15, risk_bounds=c(0.01,0.70),
  nscenarios=50, config=cfg, method=methods, nsim=1000, seed=42)
print(head(panel$scenarios, 6), digits=5)
print(panel$aggregate, digits=5, row.names=FALSE)
cases.interpretation: For this setting, dose 2 is fixed at 0.25, dose 1 at 0.15, and dose 3 at 0.40. Dose 4 is a uniform draw between 0.40 and 0.70. The run contains 50 x 1000 x 6 = 300,000 simulated trials. Aggregate means equally weight the 50 scenario estimates; their SD describes between-scenario dispersion, including finite-trial noise, not Monte Carlo SE.

cases.title: 10. Draw spaghetti comparisons and inspect the audit table
cases.code:
comparison <- plot_spaghetti(panel, method="combined", comparator="tite_boin",
                              metric="accuracy_pct", relative_gap=0.10,
                              target=0.25)
print(head(comparison, 6), digits=5)
print(table(comparison$direction))

Blue means the first method is better by at least 10% relative to the larger estimate; red means the comparator is better; gray means a smaller gap. Higher accuracy is better. For DLT burden or duration, lower is better. Colors are descriptive, not significance tests.

cases.title: 11. Include all-too-toxic cases and both upper gaps
cases.code:
boundary <- simulate_random_scenarios(ndoses=4, mtd=c(0,2),
  upper_gap=c(0.15,0.20), lower_gap=0.10, nscenarios=5,
  config=cfg, method=c("bold","combined","tite_boin"),
  nsim=1000, seed=42)
print(boundary$settings[c(1,6,11,16),], row.names=FALSE)
print(boundary$aggregate[c("method","mtd","upper_gap","n_scenarios",
                           "accuracy_pct","accuracy_sd","actual_dlts")],
      digits=5, row.names=FALSE)
cases.interpretation: This executes 5 scenarios for each MTD/gap combination, including MTD=0. For all-too-toxic cases, correct selection is no dose; they are not dropped. The setting-specific mean and SD must not be pooled indiscriminately across different MTD categories or gaps.
